subject.title: [Bug]: Secret provider crash-loop exhausts 1Password service account rate limits

question: What startup policy should OpenClaw use when an active exec-backed SecretRef fails under a supervisor restart loop?
rationale: Automation should not choose between fail-fast security posture, bounded retry/backoff, degraded startup, circuit breaking, or new config because those choices affect credential safety, availability, and operator recovery behavior.

options.title: Bounded generic retry first
options.body: Add a small core retry/backoff policy for startup SecretRef activation failures, with clear logs and tests, while avoiding provider-specific 1Password behavior and avoiding new config unless maintainers decide it is needed.

options.title: Keep fail-fast and document supervisor limits
options.body: Preserve the current fail-closed startup contract and add stronger doctor/docs guidance for launchd/systemd restart throttling and external secret-provider wrappers.

options.title: Design degraded startup or circuit breaker
options.body: Allow selected gateway surfaces to come up without unavailable secrets or stop retrying after repeated failures, but require a larger security and compatibility design before implementation.

recommendation.title: Bounded generic retry first
recommendation.body: Add a small core retry/backoff policy for startup SecretRef activation failures, with clear logs and tests, while avoiding provider-specific 1Password behavior and avoiding new config unless maintainers decide it is needed.

likelyOwner.reason: The SecretRef provider/runtime snapshot design and the prior broad expansion PR make this the strongest routing signal for the policy decision.
